title: Hypothesis (S) for tame types via Bernstein + [KY]
body_html:
Hypothesis (S) for tame types

Proposition. For the tame Yu/AFMO data, $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ is a direct summand of $\Rep(G)$ — in particular a Serre subcategory.
proof_html:
By the Bernstein decomposition $\Rep(G) = \prod_{\mathfrak s} \Rep^{\mathfrak s}(G)$, $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ is a Serre subcategory iff the indexing set of Bernstein components matching $\Phi$ is closed under the Bernstein-equivalence relation. Two routes give this:

Route 1 (Kim–Yu). [Kim–Yu, Thm 6.3] (also stated as Yu/AFMO classification) gives an explicit bijection between Bernstein components of $\Rep(G)$ and equivalence classes of tame generic cuspidal data $(\vec G, (x, \{\iota\}), \vec r, \rho, \vec\phi)$ for the depth-zero Levi $G^{(0)} = M$. Components matching a given $\Phi = (\mathscr K_+, \phi)$ are precisely those with $\vec\phi|{\mathscr K+}$ in the equivalence class of $\phi$; this is manifestly a union of Bernstein blocks, hence a direct factor and a Serre subcategory.

Route 2 (Dat–Fintzen, modern). [Dat–Fintzen 2026 §2] gives the wild-inertia parameter version: Bernstein components of $\Rep(G)$ correspond to wild-inertia equivalence classes $\iota \in I_x / \sim_x$, and the categories $\Rep^{\phi, I}_R(G)$ they introduce (§2.7) are defined block-by-block. Their Theorem 2.7.1 proves the Serre-subcategory property in this framework. Specializing the wild-inertia parameter to our single semisimple character $\phi$ (treating $I = \{\iota\}$ as a singleton class) gives back our $\Rep_\Phi(G)$, with the same Serre property. $\square$

Either route closes (S); both rely on the corrected Yu construction (Fintzen 2021; see Fintzen 2021: correction to Yu's tame supercuspidal construction) which guarantees that the cuspidal data $(\vec G, (x, {\iota}), \vec r, \rho, \vec\phi)$ produce actual supercuspidals, ensuring the Bernstein bijection is well-defined.

Combined with [[node:applications.tame_T_axioms]] and [[node:applications.tame_hypotheses_K]] this verifies all hypotheses of Main Theorem 8.2.1: Rep_Φ(G) ≃ Rep_0(M) in the tame setting.
